sections.title: General Definitions 42
paragraphs: Accepted Agricultural Practices (AAPs): Accepted practices for agriculture, including farm 44 structures other than dwellings, as currently defined by the Secretary of the Vermont Agency of 45 Agriculture, Food and Markets (see exemptions under Section 10.2). See also Agriculture, Farm 1 Structure. 2 Accepted Management Practices (AMPs): Accepted practices for silviculture (forestry) as 4 currently defined by the Commissioner of the Vermont Department or Forests, Parks and 5 Recreation (see exemptions under Section 10.2). See also Forestry. 6 Access: A defined area of ingress and/or egress between a property and an abutting road right-8 of-way (e.g., a curb cut) or a surface water. See also Driveway, Road. 9 Accessory Dwelling: See Dwelling, Accessory. 11 Accessory Structure, Use: A structure or use that is clearly incidental, customary, and 13 subordinate in size and overall appearance (except for barns) to the principal structure or use of 14 land on the same lot. Examples: in-ground pools, ponds, garages, storage sheds, playhouses, 15 tree houses, barns, satellite dishes, residential wind towers, etc. See also Dwelling, Accessory 16 and Structure. 17 Act: 24 V.S.A., Chapter 117, the Vermont Municipal and Regional Planning and Development 19 Act as most recently amended. 20 Adaptive Reuse: The rehabilitation or renovation of an existing historic structure, as listed on 22 the Vermont Historic Sites and Structures Survey for the Town of Underhill, the National 23 Register of Historic Places, or another list prepared and maintained by the town for this 24 purpose, for another use as specified in these regulations (see Section 4.2). 25 Administrative Officer: The Underhill Zoning Administrator. 27 Affordable Housing: Housing that is either: (1) owned by its inhabitants, whose gross annual 29 household income does not exceed 80 percent of the median income for the Burlington 30 Metropolitan Statistical Area, as defined by the United States Department of Housing and 31 Urban Development, and the total annual cost of the housing, including principal, interest, 32 taxes and insurance, is not more than 30 percent of the household's gross annual income; or (2) 33 rented by its inhabitants whose gross annual household income does not exceed 80 percent of 34 the median income for the Burlington Metropolitan Statistical Area, as defined by the United 35 States Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the total annual cost of the 36 housing, including rent, utilities, and condominium association fees, is not more than 30 37 percent of the household's gross annual income. "Perpetually affordable" shall mean housing 38 that meets the affordability requirements of these regulations for a minimum period of 99 39 years from the date of first sale or lease. 40 Affordable Housing Development: A housing development in which at least 20% of the units, 42 or a minimum of five units, whichever is greater, are affordable housing units. 43 Agribusiness: An enterprise that supplies raw materials, feed, equipment or supporting 1 services to agricultural producers, or engages in the collection, processing, storage and 2 distribution of agricultural commodities. An agribusiness may be established on an operating 3 farm, subject to these regulations. 4 Agriculture: As defined by the Vermont Secretary of Agriculture, Food and Markets, to include 6 the cultivation or other use of land for growing food, fiber, Christmas trees, maple sap, or 7 horticultural and orchard crops; the raising, feeding or management of livestock, poultry, 8 equines, fish or bees; the operation of greenhouses; the production of maple sap; the on-site 9 storage, preparation and sale of agricultural products principally produced on the farm; and the 10 on-site production of fuel or power from agricultural products or wastes produced on the farm. 11 The term shall also include commercial boarding and riding stables. See also Accepted 12 Agricultural Practices, Farm Structure. 13 Agricultural Products: Products produced, prepared and/or processed from an agricultural 15 operation including but not limited to milk, vegetables, fruits, flowers, potting or bedding 16 plants, soil or compost, trees, shrubs, greens, maple syrup or other sap products, meat, poultry, 17 eggs, fish, honey, and other bee products. This also includes products manufactured from 18 these products, including cheese and other dairy products. See also Agriculture. 19 Agricultural Structure: See Farm Structure. 21 Agritourism: Activities conducted on a working farm and offered to the public or invited groups 23 for the purposes of recreation, education, or active involvement in farm operations. Activities 24 must be clearly related and incidental to on-site farming operations, and may include farm 25 tours, hayrides, petting zoos, classes related to agricultural products or skills, tastings, the sale 26 of farm products, and associated facilities. Guest accommodations may be provided on-site in 27 association with a bed and breakfast or inn established under these regulations. 28 Alpine Ski Facility: An area and facility developed for downhill skiing, with trails and lifts, which 30 may also include associated ticketing, parking, ski equipment sales and rentals, ski instruction, 31 safety, patrol, snowmaking and maintenance facilities, and warming hut facilities to be 32 accessed primarily by ski trails or service roads. Other facilities, such as commercial lodging, 33 indoor recreation, cultural and restaurant facilities, which may support year-round use, may be 34 allowed in association with an alpine ski facility subject to review as a mixed use (see Section 35 4.12) or a planned unit development (Article IX). 36 Alteration: Any relocation, structural change, rearrangement, or addition to a building or 38 structure, excluding normal maintenance and repair activities. Alterations shall include any 39 construction that changes the number of dwelling units, or increases the size of a building or 40 structure, including its height, length, width, footprint, or gross floor area. It shall also include 41 any increase in the number of bedrooms or bathrooms. See also Conversion, Improvement, 42 Substantial Improvement. 43 Applicant: The owner of land or property proposed to be subdivided and/or developed in 1 accordance with these regulations or his or her duly authorized representative. Any party with 2 a legal interest in land subdivision and/or development may apply for a permit in cooperation 3 with the owner of the property. See also Authorized Agent, Interested Person. 4 Approval: A written decision issued by the Underhill Development Review Board within the 6 statutory time limit, or in the event of the DRB's failure to act within the specified time limit, a 7 certification of such failure to act issued by the Municipal Clerk, as attached to the permit 8 application and recorded in the land records of the municipality. 9 Authorized Agent: A person or group of persons who is duly authorized in writing by an 11 applicant or subdivider to act on his/her behalf. 12 Bar: See Restaurant. 14 Basement: Any area of a building having its floor at subgrade (below ground level) on all sides. 16 Bed & Breakfast (B&B): A single family dwelling occupied by the owner or operator, in which no 18 more than five guest rooms accommodating up to ten guests within the dwelling and/or in an 19 accessory structure located on the same lot, are rented out to provide overnight 20 accommodations to transient travelers. Individual cooking and eating facilities shall not be 21 provided; breakfast shall be the only meal served and shall be limited to overnight guests. The 22 bed and breakfast shall function as a private home with house guests. Parking requirements 23 also apply (see Section 4.5). See also Commercial Lodging Facility, Inn. 24 Board: The Underhill Development Review Board, as established under the Act, unless 26 otherwise specified. 27 Boundary (Lot Line) Adjustment: A change in the location of lot line(s) between adjoining 29 parcels where no new lot is created, for purposes of transferring land between adjoining 30 properties. A boundary adjustment shall not create a nonconforming lot or use (see Section 31 7.2). See also Subdivision. 32 Buffer: Any space between adjoining land uses or between a land use and a natural feature, 34 which is intended and designed to reduce the impact of one use on the other use or feature. 35 Buffers may include open space, woodland, landscaped areas, undisturbed vegetated areas, or 36 other types of physical, visual or sound barriers. 37 Building: A structure having a roof supported by columns or walls and intended for the shelter 39 or accommodation of persons, animals, goods, chattel or equipment. See also Structure. 40 Building Coverage: As specified by zoning district to mean either (1) that portion (percentage) 42 of a lot area which is covered by buildings and other structures, to be calculated as the sum of 43 all building or structure footprints divided by the lot area: (total building footprint/lot area) x 44 100 = % building coverage, or (2) the maximum total building footprint allowed per lot, to be 1 calculated based on the sum of all building and structure footprints on that lot. 2 Building Envelope: Designated area(s) on a lot within which structures, parking and loading 4 areas shall be located; and outside of which structures, parking or loading areas shall not be 5 located. At minimum the building envelope shall be defined by required district setbacks and 6 height limits; but may be also defined, as specified under these regulations, to exclude other 7 portions of the lot (e.g., steep slopes, surface waters, wetlands, required buffer areas, 8 designated open space). 9 Building Height: See Height. 11 Building Orientation: The location on a lot of a building or other structure in relation to road 13 rights-of-way and, where present, adjoining and facing structures and/or designated open 14 space areas, such as a common park or green. 15 Camp: A type of detached, seasonal dwelling unit which is not the primary residence of the 17 owner or occupant, is occupied only on a part-time or seasonal basis, and which is structurally 18 not suited for year-round occupancy. This definition shall include (1) a dwelling which is 19 occupied no more than 180 days during any one (1) year period, and which lacks one or more of 20 the basic amenities, services or utilities required for year-round or all weather occupancy, 21 including but not limited to a winterized water system, insulated walls and roof, heating source, 22 adequate water or wastewater disposal systems, or utility line connection, or (2) a dwelling that 23 has been specifically permitted as a camp. For purposes of these regulations, a dwelling listed 24 on the Underhill Grand List as a single family vacation residence (V1 or V2) as of the effective 25 date of these regulations shall be deemed a seasonally occupied dwelling and may be deemed a 26 camp under this definition, unless it has been permitted as a single family dwelling or it has 27 been documented by the applicant and determined by the Zoning Administrator to be an 28 existing single family dwelling. See also Dwelling, Accessory and Dwelling, Single Family. 29 Camper (Recreation Vehicle): Any vehicle used as temporary sleeping, camping or living 31 quarters, which is mounted on wheels, a truck or a camper body, or towed by a motor vehicle, 32 and includes a holding tank for the storage of sewage if bathroom facilities are present. This 33 definition includes recreation vehicles such as motor homes and travel trailers, but specifically 34 excludes tiny houses (see Section 3.22) and mobile homes (see Section 4.3). See also Mobile 35 Home, "Recreation Vehicle" as defined for purposes of flood hazard area management and 36 regulation under Section 11.3. 37 Campground: A parcel of land upon which three or more cabins, lean-tos or yurts, or three or 39 more campsites for occupancy by a camper or tent, are located as temporary, seasonal living 40 quarters for recreation, education, or vacation purposes (see Section 4.4). See also Camper. 41 Capacity Study: An inventory of available natural and man-made resources (e.g., facilities, 43 services), based on detailed data collection, which identifies the capacities and limits of those 44 resources to absorb land development, as defined under the Act [S4303]. 45 Cemetery: Land used or dedicated to the burial of the dead, including cremains. A cemetery 2 may include as accessory structures an office, a chapel, mausoleums, columbaria, and 3 maintenance facilities. An individual burial site on private land, registered with the Underhill 4 Town Clerk in accordance with state law, is exempted from this definition. See also Funeral 5 Home. 6 Change of Use: See Conversion. 8 Character of the Area: For purposes of these regulations, the "character of the area" or 10 character of a neighborhood is the planned type, density and pattern of development for a 11 particular area or neighborhood, as defined by zoning district purpose statements and clearly-12 stated goals, policies and objectives of the Underhill Town Plan that are specific to that area 13 and/or the physical circumstances of development. 14 Clearing: The removal of existing vegetation, e.g., as part of site preparation for the installation 16 of driveways, septic systems, building sites and construction or yard areas. 17 Commercial Lodging Facility: For the purposes of these regulations a bed and breakfast or an 19 inn (see Section 4.5). See Bed & Breakfast, Inn. 20 Commercial Use: An occupation, employment or enterprise that is carried on for profit by the 22 owner, lessee or licensee. 23 Commission: The Underhill Planning Commission, as established under the Act, unless 25 otherwise specified. 26 Common Land: Land within a development or subdivision that is not individually owned, but 28 which is designed to be held in common for the use, enjoyment, management and maintenance 29 by the residents or occupants of a development or subdivision. Common land may include but 30 not be limited to open space areas, parking lots, community water and wastewater systems, 31 pedestrian walkways, utility and road rights-of way. 32 Community Center: A building used for recreational, social, and cultural activities which is not 34 operated for profit and is intended primarily to serve the residents of the town or the 35 development in which it is located. 36 Community System (Water, Wastewater): Any water or wastewater disposal system other 38 than a municipally-owned system which provides potable water to or disposes of wastewater 39 from two or more domestic, commercial, industrial, or institutional uses. Such systems shall 40 include associated collection, distribution and treatment facilities. 41 Conditional Use: A use, which because of its nature and potential impacts to roads, traffic, 43 community facilities and services, adjoining properties and uses, or the character of the area, 44 may be allowed with conditions only upon approval of the Development Review Board. 45 Condominium: A form of ownership of real property that includes separate, individual 2 ownership of portions of the property (e.g., units in an apartment building) and undivided or 3 joint ownership of the remainder of the property (e.g., common areas, common land, shared 4 infrastructure). For purposes of these regulations, condominium development can be in the 5 form of a two-family dwelling or multi-family dwelling, and must meet the same requirements 6 as other types of land subdivision and development. See also Dwelling, Multi-family. 7 Conformance with the Plan: A subdivision or development that conforms to or implements 9 specifically stated goals and policies of the Underhill Town Plan currently in effect; i.e., that, 10 under the Act [S4303]: 11 (1) Makes progress toward attaining, or at least does not interfere with plan goals and policies, 13 (2) Provides for proposed land uses, densities and intensities of development contained in the 14 municipal plan. 15 (3) Carries out, as applicable, specific proposals for community facilities, or other proposed 16 actions contained in the municipal plan. 17 Construction Drawings: Drawings showing the as-built location, profile grades, size and types of 19 drains, sewers, water mains, underground fire alarm ducts, underground power and telephone 20 ducts, pavements, cross sections of streets, miscellaneous structures, etc. 21 Contiguous Land: (1) A parcel of land contained within a single, unbroken parcel boundary; or 23 (2) two or more parcels which share a common parcel boundary or point. Where one or more 24 existing road rights-of-way bisect an existing parcel, the right(s)-of-way may be considered a 25 boundary dividing the parcel into two or more lots only if all portions of the parcel divided by 26 the right(s)-of-way meet the minimum lot size requirement for the district in which they are 27 located. 28 Contractor's Yard: A parcel of land with or without buildings thereon to be used for the storage 30 of equipment, materials, and/or vehicles used in the operation of construction and related 31 trades (see Section 4.6). See also Home Industry. 32 Conversion: A change in the existing use of land or a structure to a different use, with or 34 without structural alteration. This includes but may not be limited to the conversion of camps 35 or accessory dwellings to single family dwellings, or the conversion of a single family dwelling to 36 a two-family or multi-family dwelling (see Section 3.3). See also Adaptive Reuse. 37 Coverage: See Building Coverage, Lot Coverage. 39 Cul-de-Sac: A road intersecting another road at one end, and terminated at the other end by a 41 vehicular turnaround. 42 Cultural Facility: A museum, theater, concert hall, library or other establishment offering 1 programs, performances or exhibits or cultural, educational, historical, or scientific interest, 2 excluding movie theaters as a principal use. See also Recreation, Indoor. 3 Curb Cut: See Access. 4 Day Care Facility: An establishment, except as supported in whole by tax funds, operated as a 6 business or service on a regular or continual basis, whether for compensation or not, which 7 provides care, protection, supervision and/or education for children or adults for periods of less 8 than 24 hours. This definition shall include all facilities that are required to be licensed by the 9 State of Vermont as a private kindergarten, nursery school, and/or day care facility except for 10 home child care facilities (see Section 4.7). See also Group Home, Home Child Care, Residential 11 Care Facility. 12 Deer Yard: An area designated by the Vermont Department of Fish and Wildlife as wintering 14 habitat for white tailed deer. 15 Degree of Nonconformance: The degree to which a structure, or portion thereof, does not 17 meet required dimensional standards (e.g., minimum setback distances) as specified in these 18 regulations. For purposes of these regulations, any enlargement or other structural alteration 19 which extends the footprint, height or volume of a structure within a required setback distance, 20 or above the maximum allowed height (i.e., the amount of encroachment), shall be considered 21 to increase the degree of noncompliance. See also Nonconforming Structure. 22 Demolition: The razing of more than 50% of a structure. 24 Density: The maximum number of dwelling units or gross square footage of building per acre of 26 lot area, excluding the land area within existing and proposed road rights-of-way. 27 Development: See Land Development. Also see DEVELOPMENT as defined for purposes of 29 flood hazard area management and regulation under Section 11.3. 30 Development Right: The right to build or develop on a specific parcel of land in accordance with 32 these regulations for the district in which the parcel is located. 33 DRB: Underhill Development Review Board as established under the Act. 35 Drive-through: An establishment which, by design, physical facilities, and/or service 37 encourages or permits customers to receive services, obtain goods, or be entertained while 38 remaining in their motor vehicles. 39 Driveway: A private travel way, including an easement or right-of-way serving up to three (3) 41 parcels, which provides vehicular access to a parking area(s) associated with the principal 42 structure or use (see Section 3.2). See also Access, Road. 43 Dwelling, Accessory: A secondary dwelling unit established in conjunction with and clearly 1 subordinate to a single family dwelling, which is retained in common ownership, is located 2 within, attached to or on the same lot as the primary dwelling, and which otherwise meets 3 applicable requirements of these regulations (see Section 4.15). See also Dwelling, Two-Family. 4 Dwelling, Seasonal: See Camp. 6 Dwelling, Multi-Family: A building or portion thereof containing three (3) or more dwelling 8 units. See also Dwelling Unit; Dwelling, Two Family; and Condominium. 9 Dwelling, Single Family: (1) A detached building containing one (1) principal dwelling unit, and 11 up to one (1) accessory dwelling as allowed under Section 4.15. See also Dwelling, Accessory 12 and Group Home. 13 Dwelling, Two-Family: A detached building, such as a duplex or condominium, that contains 15 two principal dwelling units. 16 Dwelling Unit: A building, or portion thereof, designed, constructed, or used as separate living 18 quarters for one (1) family, including any domestic employees employed on the premises, 19 which includes food preparation, sleeping and sanitary facilities. This definition specifically 20 excludes boarding or rooming houses, residential care facilities, inns and hotels. See also 21 Family. 22 Dwelling Unit, Affordable: See Affordable Housing. 24 Dwelling Unit, Elderly: See Elderly Housing. 26 Easement: A legal right (such as a right of way) or interest in land owned by another that 28 entitles the holder to limited use or enjoyment of a designated portion(s) of the property for a 29 specified purpose. 30 Easement, Conservation: A type of easement that restricts land development, including the 32 subdivision or development of land, as necessary to protect specified conservation resources or 33 values. 34 Elderly Housing: Housing development that meets one or more of the following requirements, 36 in accordance with the Federal Fair Housing Act: (1) Housing specifically designed for and 37 occupied by elderly persons under a federal or state housing program. (2) Housing occupied 38 only by persons who are 62 years or older. (3) A housing development in which 80% or more of 39 the dwelling units are to be occupied by at least one person who is 55 or older, under adopted 40 policies to house persons who are 55 years or older. Elderly housing may include, as 41 accessories, congregate dining and recreational facilities and assisted living services. See also 42 Residential Care Facility. 43 Elevation Limit: The prohibition of new structures or changes in the use of existing structures 1 above 1500 feet in elevation (from mean sea level). 2 Enlargement: Any increase in the height or the footprint of a structure, e.g., through 4 extensions or additions. 5 Extraction: A use involving the on-site removal of surface and subsurface materials, including 7 soil, sand, gravel, and stone. Typical uses include sand and gravel pits and related operations 8 such as the crushing, screening, and temporary storage of materials on-site (see Section 4.8). 9 See also Quarrying. 10 Family: One or more persons related by blood, marriage, civil union, adoption other form of 12 legal guardianship as recognized by the State of Vermont, or a group of not more than eight 13 unrelated persons, exclusive of domestic servants, living together as a household. See also 14 Group Home. 15 Farm Structure: (1) In accordance with the Act [S 4413(d)], a building, enclosure or fence for 17 housing livestock, raising horticultural or agronomic plants, or carrying out other practices 18 associated with accepted agricultural or farming practices, including a silo; but excludes a 19 dwelling for human habitation. (2) As defined by the Vermont Secretary of Agriculture under 20 accepted agricultural practices, a farm structure includes a structure used for agricultural 21 production, which meets one or more of the following: (a) is used in connection with the sale 22 of $1000 or more of agricultural products in a normal year; (b) is used in connection with the 23 raising, feeding and management of the minimum specified number of adult animals: four (4) 24 equines, five (5) cattle or bison, 15 swine, 15 goats, 15 sheep, 15 fallow or red deer, 50 turkeys 25 or geese, 100 laying hens or ducks, 250 broilers, pheasant, Chukar partridge or Coturnix quail, 26 three (3) camelids, four (4) ratites, 30 rabbits, or 1000 pounds of cultured trout; (c) is used by a 27 farmer filing with the Internal Revenue Service a 1040(F) income tax statement in at least one 28 of the past two years; (d) is on a farm with a business and farm management plan approved by 29 the Secretary. See also Agriculture, Accepted Agricultural Practices. 30 Fence: An assemblage of materials, which may include metal, stone, wood, or any 32 combination, erected and placed on the ground for purposes of limiting visual or physical 33 access, and/or to mark a property boundary. Agricultural and residential fences or walls less 34 than six feet in height which do not obstruct public rights-of-way are specifically exempted 35 from these regulations (see Sections 3.5 and 10.2). For purposes of these regulations, other 36 fences shall be considered a type of accessory structure. 37 Fill: Deposit or placement of earth, sand, gravel, rock or other similar material. 39 Financial Institution: A bank, savings and loan, finance, mortgage or investment company. 41 Floor Area, Gross: The total area of all floors of a building as measured to the outside surfaces 43 of exterior walls, including halls, stairways, elevator shafts, attached garages, enclosed porches 44 and balconies, but excluding interior vehicular parking and loading spaces, or any space where 1 the floor to ceiling height is less than six feet. 2 Forestry: The use and management of timber land for purposes of conservation and/or wood 4 production and timber harvesting. This definition specifically excludes sawmills, lumber yards 5 and other similar facilities used for the processing and/or manufacturing of wood and wood 6 products, with the exception of portable sawmills and other equipment used on site in 7 association with timber harvesting activities. See also Accepted Management Practices. Light 8 Industry. 9 Frequency: The number of cycles completed each second by an electromagnetic wave 11 measured in hertz (Hz). 12 Front Lot Line: The dividing line between a lot and a public or private road, defined along the 14 edge of the road right-of-way between side lot lines. For purposes of these regulations, a lot 15 without frontage along a road-right-of-way shall have only side lot lines. See also Lot Frontage. 16 Frontage: See Lot Frontage. 18 Funeral Home: A building or part thereof used for funeral services. Such building may also 20 contain space and facilities for the preparation of the dead for interment or cremation, 21 crematoriums, the performance of autopsies and associated surgical procedures, the storage 22 and sale of caskets, funeral urns and related funeral supplies, and the storage of funeral 23 vehicles. 24 Garage Sale: The casual sale or offering at any one time of new, used, or second hand items of 26 tangible personal property to the general public, which is generally advertised by such terms 27 "garage sale," "yard sale," "rummage sale," "attic sale," "lawn sale," "porch sale," "barn sale" or 28 similar phrase (see Exemptions under Section 10.2). See also Outdoor Market. 29 Garden Center: The use of land, buildings and/or structures for the purpose of selling lawn and 31 garden equipment, furnishings and supplies. This definition specifically does not include 32 nurseries and greenhouses that are defined as "Agriculture" or "Accepted Agricultural 33 Practices" and are therefore exempted from these regulations. See also Agriculture, Accepted 34 Agricultural Practices. 35 Gas Station: Any lot or area of land including the building or buildings thereon, which is used 37 for the sale of motor vehicle fuels, lubricants, and related motor vehicles products, and/or 38 which has facilities for fueling, washing or servicing motor vehicles (see Section 4.9). This 39 definition includes gas stations and car washes; but specifically excludes automobile and motor 40 vehicle repair services and sales, and the sale of food and unrelated convenience or grocery 41 items. See also Motor Vehicle Sales & Service, Mixed Use. 42 Grade, Finished: Completed surface of grounds, lawns, walks, paved areas and roads which 44 have been brought to grades as shown in associated plans. 45 Grade, Natural: The initial, original or pre-development surface of ground within a proposed 2 building or structure footprint, as measured from contour elevations prior to any site clearing, 3 filling or excavation. 4 Greenhouse: A commercial agricultural business or farm structure for growing flowering and 6 other plants for wholesale or retail sale on the premises. Residential greenhouses, for purposes 7 of these regulations, are considered accessory structures. See also Accepted Agriculture 8 Practices, Agriculture, Farm Structure, Garden Center. 9 Grocery Store: A self-service retail establishment with a gross floor area of 4,000 square feet or 11 more that sells primarily food and household goods. For purposes of these regulations, grocery 12 stores of less than 4,000 square feet (e.g., convenience, neighborhood or general stores), shall 13 be separately defined and regulated as retail stores. See also Retail Store. 14 Group Home: In accordance with the Act [S4412(1)], a residential care home operating under 16 state licensing or registration, which serves not more than eight (8) persons who have a 17 handicap or disability as defined in state statutes (9 V.S.A. 4501), and meets the requirements 18 of Section 4.10. See also Residential Care Facility. 19 Health Clinic: A building or part thereof operated by physicians, surgeons, dentists, 21 chiropractors, therapists, or other licensed health care professionals for the examination and 22 treatment of patients on an out-patient basis. This definition does not include a public or 23 private hospital, or the professional office of a licensed health care provider located in his or 24 her residence. See also Home Occupation, Health Care Facility. 25 Height: The distance above ground of a structure as measured vertically from the average 27 finished grade at the base of the structure to the highest point of the structure or roof surface, 28 excluding the chimney (see Section 3.6). See also Grade, Finished. 29 Historic Resource: A site, structure or other cultural feature that is (1) listed on, or eligible for 31 listing on national or state registers of historic places, or (2) identified as having local historical 32 significance in the Underhill Town Plan, historic resource inventories, or through site 33 investigation. Historic resources include, but may not be limited to buildings, structures and 34 their surroundings (context), historic and prehistoric archaeological sites, and historic landscape 35 features (e.g., witness/survey trees, stone walls, fence lines, foundations and cellar holes). 36 Home Child Care: A home-based child daycare business, the owner and operator of which is 38 licensed or registered by the state, which is considered to constitute a permitted single family 39 residential use of property in accordance with the Act [S4412(5)] (see Section 4.7). See also 40 Day Care Facility. 41 Home Industry: An expanded home-based business conducted by one or more residents of a 43 single family dwelling and up to five nonresident employees, which is carried on within the 44 principal dwelling, accessory structure and/or designated yard areas, and meets all applicable 1 requirements of these regulations (see Section 4.11). See also Home Occupation. 2 Home Occupation: A use conducted entirely within a minor portion of a single family dwelling 4 or accessory structure to the dwelling, by one or more residents of the dwelling and up to two 5 nonresident employees, which is clearly incidental and secondary to the use of the dwelling for 6 dwelling purposes, and which does not change the character thereof (see Section 4.11). See 7 also Bed & Breakfast, Home Child Care, Home Industry. 8 Improvement: Any physical addition to real property, or any part of such addition, including but 10 not limited to any building, structure, infrastructure, parking facility, wall, fencing, or 11 landscaping (see also Substantial Improvement). See also Public Improvement, Substantial 12 Improvement. 13 Infrastructure: Facilities and services required to support residential, commercial, industrial 15 and civic land development, which may include but not be limited to roads, sidewalks and other 16 transportation facilities; water, wastewater, and stormwater management systems; 17 communications, electrical and other utilities; and public facilities such as fire houses, parks, 18 and schools. For purposes of these regulations, infrastructure is considered and regulated as 19 land development, which may be principal, accessory or incidental to other types of land 20 development. See also Development, Improvement, Public Facility, Structure. 21 Inn: A type of commercial lodging facility consisting of a building or group of buildings 23 containing a maximum of 24 guest rooms for occupancy and use by transients on a short-term 24 basis (less than one month on average), and may include common dining, meeting, event, 25 recreation and service facilities for the use of guests (see Section 4.5). Dining, meeting, event, 26 and recreation facilities open to the general public may be allowed as a mixed use, subject to 27 review as a mixed use, in zoning districts in which all such uses are allowed. See also Bed & 28 Breakfast, Commercial Lodging Facility, Mixed Use. 29 Institutional Facility: A type of public facility, including buildings and land, that for purposes of 31 these regulations is limited to large facilities that may include group housing and that are 32 owned, operated or contracted by a public agency or nonprofit entity for a public purpose. 33 Such institutional facilities may include college campuses, hospitals or prison facilities. See also 34 Cultural Facility, Public Facility, Residential Care Home. 35 Interested Person: As defined under the Act [S4465], for purposes of appeals: 37 (1) A person owning title to property, or a municipality or solid waste district empowered to 38 condemn it or an interest in it, affected by these regulations, who alleges that the regulations 39 impose on the property unreasonable or inappropriate restrictions of present or potential use 40 under the particular circumstances of the case. 41 (2) The Town of Underhill or an adjoining municipality. 42 (3) A person owning or occupying property in the immediate neighborhood of a property that is 43 the subject of any decision or act taken under these regulations, who can demonstrate a 44 physical or environmental impact on the person's interest under the criteria reviewed, and who 45 alleges that the decision or act, if confirmed, will not be in accord with the policies, purposes or 1 terms of the plan or bylaws of the town. 2 (4) Any 10 persons who may be any combination of voters or real property owners within the 3 town or an adjoining municipality who, by signed petition to the Development Review Board, 4 the plan or regulations of which are at issue in any appeal brought under these regulations, 5 allege that any relief requested by a person under these regulations, if granted, will not be in 6 accord with the policies, purposes or terms of the municipal plan or regulations. The petition to 7 the Board must designate one person to serve as the representative of the petitioners 8 regarding all matters related to the appeal. 9 (5) Any department and administrative subdivision of the state owning property or any interest 10 in property within the town or an adjoining municipality, and the Agency of Commerce and 11 Community Development. 12 Junk: Any scrap or waste material which is collected, stored, handled, kept, or intended for 14 salvage, resale or conversion to another use. This includes junk motor vehicles, scrap metal, 15 plastic and rubber debris, rope, rags, batteries, paper, waste, trash or other discarded, 16 dismantled, wrecked, scrapped or ruined items or materials. 17 Junk Motor Vehicle: A discarded, dismantled, wrecked, scrapped, or ruined motor vehicle or 19 parts thereof, or a motor vehicle, other than an on-premise utility vehicle, which is allowed to 20 remain unregistered or uninspected for a period of 90 days from the date of discovery. 21 Junk Yard: See Salvage Yard. 23 Kennel: Any premises in which the care, boarding, breeding, grooming, or training of four (4) or 25 more dogs, cats, or other domestic animals is done for primarily commercial or monetary 26 purposes. See also Veterinary Clinic. 27 Land Development: The construction, reconstruction, conversion, structural alteration, 29 relocation or enlargement of any building or other structure, or of any mining operation, 30 excavation or landfill, and any change in the use of any building or other structure, land or 31 extension of use of land [24 V.S.A. S4303(10)]. See also Subdivision. Also see "Development" as 32 defined for purposes of flood hazard area management and regulation under Section 11.3. 33 Level of Service (LOS): A measure used by engineers, most commonly to rate transportation 35 infrastructure (highway, intersection) efficiency (e.g., from the Highway Capacity Manual, 36 published by the Transportation Research Board). Transportation LOS systems rate 37 performance using the letters A through F, with A being the best rating, C the average rating, 38 and F the worst rating. Highway LOS is determined based on the efficiency of traffic flow; 39 intersection LOS is based on vehicle delays (wait times) at signalized or unsignalized 40 intersections. 41 Light Industry: A facility not exceeding 10,000 square feet in total gross floor area, used for the 43 manufacture, processing, fabrication, testing and/or assembly of products. This may also 44 include associated research and development, warehousing and shipping activities. A light 45 industry shall meet all applicable requirements of these regulations, including performance 1 standards. The processing of agricultural products produced on the premises where produced 2 shall not be deemed to be manufacturing. See also Home Industry, Sawmill. 3 Loading Area: One or more spaces logically and conveniently located for bulk pickups and 5 deliveries, scaled to delivery vehicles expected to be used. Required off-street loading areas 6 are not to be included as off-street parking spaces in the computation of required off-street 7 parking space (see Section 3.13). 8 Lot: A parcel of land. For purposes of these regulations, a lot is (1) any parcel of land which has 10 sufficient area to meet the dimensional requirements of these regulations, excluding existing or 11 proposed road rights-of-way; (2) a parcel of land defined by property lines, as shown on a site 12 plan or subdivision plat. See also Contiguous Land; Lot Area; Lot, Existing; and Lot of Record. 13 Lot Area (Lot Size): The total land area within the boundaries (lot lines) of a lot, exclusive of the 15 area designated for any existing or proposed road rights-of-way as measured within the 16 boundaries of the right-of-way. 17 Lot, Corner: A lot at the junction of and abutting on two or more intersecting roads where the 19 interior angle of the intersection does not exceed 135 degrees. A lot abutting a curved street 20 shall be deemed a corner lot if the tangents to the curve are the points of intersection of the 21 side lot lines with the street lines intersect at an interior angle of less than 135 degrees. 22 Lot, Through: A lot that extends between adjoining lots and has frontage on two roads. 24 Through lots have front and side lot lines, but no rear lot line. 25 Lot Coverage: That portion (percentage) of a lot area which is covered by buildings, structures 27 and other man-made improvements, including parking and loading areas, access roads, service 28 areas, and other impermeable surfaces which prevent the infiltration of storm water. 29 Lot Depth: The minimum horizontal distance from the street line of the lot to the rear lot line of 31 such lot, as measured at right angles. 32 Lot, Existing: Any parcel in individual, separate and non-affiliated ownership from surrounding 34 properties that is legally in existence as of the effective date of these regulations. See also 35 Nonconforming Lot. 36 Lot Frontage: The front lot line along a public or private road, as measured along the road 38 right-of-way from the intersection of one side lot line to the intersection of the other lot line. 39 See also Front Lot Line. 40 Lot Line: The boundary line of a parcel of land; a property line. 42 Lot of Record: Any lot which individually, or as part of a subdivision, has been recorded in the 44 Underhill Town Office. 45 Lot Size: See Lot Area. 2 Mean Sea Level: The standard datum to which typical contour elevations are referenced. 4 Mixed Use: A building or parcel containing two (2) or more principal uses which are otherwise 6 allowed as permitted or conditional uses in the district in which the building or parcel is located 7 (see Section 4.12). Also see Planned Unit Development. 8 Mobile Home: A prefabricated single family dwelling unit which: (1) is designed for continuous 10 residential occupancy; (2) is designed to be moved on wheels, as a whole or in sections, (3) on 11 arrival at the site, is complete and ready for occupancy except for incidental unpacking, 12 assembly, and placing on supports or a permanent foundation, or installation as a unit in a 13 previously prepared structure; and (4) contains the same water supply and wastewater disposal 14 systems as immovable housing (see Section 3.4). See also Camper; Dwelling, Single Family; 15 Mobile Home Park. 16 Mobile Home Park: A parcel of land under single or common ownership or control which 18 contains, or is designed, laid out or adapted to accommodate, three (3) or more mobile homes 19 to be occupied for living purposes (see Section 3.4 and 4.13). See also Mobile Home. Also see 20 Manufactured (Mobile) Home Park as defined for purposes of flood hazard area management 21 and regulation under Section 11.3. 22 Mobile Home Sales: An establishment, including land and/or a building, for which the principal 24 use is the sale of mobile homes. This may include customary accessory structures or uses, such 25 as an office, an enclosed sales room, and a parking area. 26 Motor Vehicles Sales & Service: An establishment, including land and buildings, for which the 28 principal use is the sale and repair of automobiles or other motor vehicles, to include the sale 29 and/or leasing of motor vehicles and accessory products, general vehicle and engine repair 30 shops, rebuilding and/or reconditioning shops, and body shops. This does not including 31 gasoline stations except as may be allowed a mixed use, or home based repair businesses (see 32

sections.title: ). See also Gas Station, Home Industry, Mixed Use. 33
paragraphs: Municipal Land Use Permit: As defined in the Act [S4303] to include, as issued by the 35 municipality: (1) final zoning, subdivision, site plan or building permits or approvals relating to 36 subdivision and land development; (2) septic or sewage system permits; (3) final official 37 minutes of meetings which relate to permits or approvals, which serve as the sole evidence of 38 such permits or approvals; (4) certificates of occupancy, compliance or similar certificates; (5) 39 certificates of location for salvage yards; and (6) any amendments to the previously listed, 40 permits, approvals and/or certificates. 41 Municipal (Town) Plan: The municipal plan for the Town of Underhill as most recently adopted 43 in accordance with the Act. See also "Conformance with the Plan." 44 Nature Center: A scientific or educational facility open to the public that provides facilities, 1 services, research, materials, educational programs, exhibits and/or displays promoting 2 understanding, sound management and protection of the natural environment. 3 Nonconforming Lot: A lot lawfully in existence as of the effective date of these regulations, 5 which does not conform within these regulations, including zoning district dimensional, density 6 or coverage requirements, or other applicable dimensional requirements of these regulations 7 (see Section 3.8). See also Nonconforming Structure, Nonconforming Use. 8 Nonconforming Structure: A structure or part thereof lawfully in existence as of the effective 10 date of these regulations, which does not conform to the provisions of these regulations, but 11 did conform to all applicable laws, ordinances and regulations prior to the enactment of these 12 regulations; and structures improperly authorized in error by the Zoning Administrator (see 13

sections.title: ). See also Nonconforming Use. 14
paragraphs: Nonconforming Use: The use of a land or structure lawfully in existence as of the effective date 16 of these regulations, which does not conform with these regulations, including but not limited 17 to allowed uses within the district in which it is located, but did conform to all applicable laws, 18 ordinances and regulations prior to the enactment of these regulations; and uses improperly 19 authorized in error by the Zoning Administrator (see Section 3.10). See also Nonconforming 20 Structure. 21 Nordic Ski Facility: An area and facility developed for cross-country and backcountry skiing 23 and snowshoeing on a maintained trail network, which may also include associated ticketing, 24 parking, ski equipment sales and rentals, ski instruction, safety, patrol, snowmaking and trail 25 maintenance facilities, and warming hut facilities to be accessed primarily by ski trails or service 26 roads. Other facilities, such as camping, commercial lodging, indoor recreation, cultural and 27 restaurant facilities, which may support year-round use, may be allowed in association with a 28 Nordic ski facility subject to review as a mixed use (see Section 4.12) or a planned unit 29 development (Article IX). 30 Nursery: See Greenhouse. 32 Office: A room, suite of rooms or building principally used for conducting the affairs of a 34 business, profession, or service industry. This definition specifically excludes office space which 35 is associated with home occupations or which is clearly accessory to another allowed principal 36 use. It also specifically excludes the on-premise retail sale of goods. See also Home Occupation. 37 Open Space: Land not occupied by structures, buildings, roads, rights-of-way, and parking lots. 39 Open space may or may not be held in common. "Usable open space" is further characterized 40 as open space which is available and accessible to all occupants of the building or buildings on 41 the lot for purposes of active or passive recreation. 42 Out Building: See Accessory Structure. 44 Outdoor Market: An occasional or periodic market held in an open area or structure where 1 groups of individual sellers offer goods for sale to the public, including "farmers" and "flea" 2 markets. See also Garage Sale. 3 Parking Facility: A separate off-street parking area, garage or similar structure that is the 5 principal use of a lot. See also Transit Facility. 6 Parking Space: An off-street area which is not less than nine feet in width and 18 feet in depth, 8 exclusive of adequate access or maneuvering area, ramps, columns, etc., which is to be used 9 exclusively as a temporary storage space for a single motor vehicle (see Section 3.13). 10 Permitted Use: An allowed use within a zoning district which requires the issuance of a zoning 12 permit by the Zoning Administrator and, depending on the type of use, site plan approval from 13 the Development Review Board (Section 5.3). See also Conditional Use. 14 Person: Any individual, partnership, corporation, association, unincorporated organization, 16 trust, or any other legal or commercial entity, including a joint venture or affiliated ownership, 17 which owns or controls land or other property to be subdivided and/or developed under the 18 provisions of these regulations. The word "person" shall also include any municipality or other 19 government agency. 20 Personal Service: A business which provides services of a personal nature, including but not 22 limited to laundry and dry cleaning, beauty and barber shops, tailoring and shoe repair, 23 photographic studios, and similar businesses. Sales of products must be clearly related and 24 incidental to services provided. See also Funeral Home. 25 Place of Worship: A building used solely for purposes of assembly and worship by a legally 27 established and recognized religious institution. This definition also includes such customary 28 accessory structures such as parish houses (see Section 4.16). See also Public Facility. 29 Planned Residential Development (PRD): A type of planned unit development specifically for 31 residential purposes in which an area of land, consisting of one or more parcels, is planned to 32 be developed as a single entity, to include residential dwelling units allowed within a zoning 33 district(s) and associated accessory structures and facilities. In a PRD, zoning district 34 dimensional standards under these regulations (Article II), including lot size, density, coverage, 35 frontage and setback requirements, may be modified or waived to provide flexibility in 36 subdivision and site design in order to promote desired types and patterns of residential 37 development (see Article IX). See also Planned Unit Development. 38 Planned Unit Development (PUD): One or more lots or parcels of land to be developed as a 40 single entity for one or more uses allowed within a zoning district(s), the plan for which may 41 propose any authorized combination of density transfers or increases, as well as a mix of land 42 uses, as allowed under these regulations. In a PUD, zoning district dimensional standards under 43 these regulations (Article II), including lot size, density, coverage, frontage and setback 44 requirements, may be modified or waived to provide flexibility in subdivision and site design in 45 order to promote desired types and patterns of mixed use development (see Article XI). See 1 also Mixed Use, Planned Residential Development. 2 Plat: A map or representation on paper, Mylar or other accepted material, of a piece of land 4 subdivided into lots and roads, drawn to scale. 5 Post Office: A facility operated by the United States Postal Service for the collection and 7 distribution of mail, and associated mailing and delivery services. 8 Primary Agricultural Soils: Agricultural soils of federal (prime), state (statewide) or local 10 importance for growing food and forage crops, as defined and mapped for the state by the 11 USDA Natural Resource Conservation Service. 12 Principal Structure: A structure or building in which the main, primary or principal use of the 14 property is conducted. Attached accessory dwellings, garages, porches or carports, or other 15 structures which share a common wall and/or roof, or are connected by an enclosed 16 breezeway, are considered to part of the principal structure. 17 Private Club: An establishment operated for social, recreational, educational or cultural 19 purposes that is open only to members and their invited guests, and not the general public. 20 Public Improvement: Any improvement which shall be owned or maintained by the Town of 22 Underhill or other government entity. 23 Public Facility: A building or other facility owned, leased, held, used, and/or controlled 25 exclusively for public purposes by a municipality, state or federal government, regulated utility 26 or railroad. Such facilities include, but may not be limited to municipal buildings and garages, 27 public parks and playgrounds, water and wastewater facilities, power generation and 28 transmission facilities, and educational facilities (see Section 4.16). 29 Quarrying: The removal of rock or minerals by means of open excavation to supply material for 31 construction, industrial or manufacturing purposes (see Section 3.4). See also Extraction. 32 Reasonable Use: A use of real property which is allowed within the district in which the 34 property is located, which provides some (but not necessarily all) potential benefit to the 35 owner, and which does not lead to unreasonable interference with another's use of property, 36 or with the natural flow of water. Reasonable use does not mean highest and best use; nor 37 does it include accessory uses, structures, or additions which may be customary, but are not 38 necessary, to the existing or intended principal use (e.g., garages, swimming pools). 39 Reconstruct: To replace or rebuild a building or structure which has been substantially 41 destroyed or demolished without regard to cause. 42 Recreation, Indoor: A building or structure designed, equipped and used for sports, leisure 44 time, and other recreational activities, except for such facilities which are accessory to an 45 approved educational facility or a residential use. This includes, but may not be limited to 1 bowling alleys, movie theaters, pool halls, skating rinks, gymnasiums, fitness centers, and 2 swimming pools. 3 Recreation, Outdoor: A facility for outdoor recreation, including but not limited to a stadium, 5 tennis courts, athletic fields, golf courses, swimming pools, and trails for hiking, horseback 6 riding, bicycling, snowmobiling, and cross-country skiing; except for such facilities which are 7 accessory to an approved educational facility or a residential use, or are otherwise exempted 8 from these regulations under Section 10.2. This definition specifically excludes separately 9 listed, defined and regulated outdoor recreation facilities, including alpine and Nordic ski 10 facilities. See also Alpine Ski Facility, Nordic Ski Facility. 11 Recreation Vehicle: See Camper. See also "Recreational Vehicle" as defined for flood hazard 13 management and regulation under Section 11.3. 14 Redemption Center: A store or other facility certified by the state [10 V.S.A. S1524] where a 16 person may, during normal business hours, redeem the amount of the deposit for an empty 17 beverage container. 18 Residential Care Facility: A facility licensed by the state which provides residential care, 20 including rooming, boarding, recreation and personal care services, to elderly or infirmed 21 individuals, on a 24-hour a day basis (see Section 4.10). See also Group Home, Institutional 22 Facility. 23 Restaurant: An establishment of which the primary function is to serve food and beverages to 25 the public for consumption only at tables or counters on the premises. This definition includes 26 cafes, bakeries with table or counter service, taverns and bars, but specifically excludes night 27 clubs. 28 Resubdivision: A change to a previously approved and recorded subdivision plat within five 30 years of the proposed subdivision Changes include, but are not limited to, changes that affect 31 any lot lines, street or road layouts, areas reserved for public use, or any map or plan that has 32 been legally recorded. 33 Retail Store: Premises where goods or merchandise are offered for retail sale to the general 35 public for personal, business, or household consumption, and where services incidental to the 36 sale of such goods are provided. This definition excludes the retail sale of gasoline and 37 automobiles and other goods and services that are otherwise more specifically addressed 38 under these regulations. See also Gasoline Station, Mobile Home Sales, Motor Vehicle Sales & 39 Service, Personal Service and Restaurant. 40 Ridgeline: The uppermost point of a ridge, hill, cliff, slope or face. It may coincide with the top 42 (highest elevation) of a rock cliff or, where the bedrock is not exposed, the most obvious break 43 in slope associated with the underlying bedrock. The term does not include intermediate 44 terraces, steps, or elevations along the face of a slope. A "prominent" ridgeline is a ridgeline 45 characterized by an elevation, slope, orientation, and/or relationship to nearby property so as 1 to be highly visible from distant vantage points. 2 Right-of-Way: (1) A formally deeded right of passage over another person's property; (2) the 4 width of the traveled and untraveled portion of a public or private road. See also Road. 5 Road: A public highway, or a private right-of-way serving four or more lots, which is designed 7 and intended for use by motor vehicles. The word "road" shall mean the entire right-of-way. 8 See also Driveway. 9 Road, Development (Private): Any road or street which is not publicly owned and maintained, 11 excluding private driveways serving up to three lots (see Section 8.6). See also Road, Driveway. 12 Road, Pent: A town highway that, under written authorization by the Underhill Selectboard, is 14 gated but not locked. 15 Road, Public: A road which is constructed within the boundaries of an officially deeded and 17 accepted public right-of-way, including municipal, state and federal highways. 18 Rock Outcrop: Portion of bedrock that protrudes through the soil, including boulders, ledges 20 and cliffs. 21 Salvage Yard: Any place of outdoor storage or deposit for storing, keeping, processing, 23 dismantling, shredding, salvaging, buying or selling discarded items, material or scrap metal. 24 This definition includes any outdoor area used for storing or keeping four or more junk vehicles, 25 excluding motor vehicle service establishments (garages) where wrecked or disabled motor 26 vehicles are stored for less than 90 days for inspection and repair (see Section 4.17). This 27 definition also does not include scrap metal crushing or processing facilities permanently 28 located on the premises or hazardous or solid waste management facilities under 10 V.S.A. 29 Chapter 159. See also Motor Vehicle Sales & Service, Public Facility, Waste Management 30 Facility. 31 Sawmill: A wood processing facility, including structures and yard areas, where logs are stored 33 and processed into lumber and other wood products. Portable chippers and sawmills used in 34 conjunction with active logging operations are excluded from this definition. See also Forestry, 35 Light Industry. 36 Scenic Resource: A landscape element or group of elements that is visually or aesthetically 38 pleasing, as viewed from a public vantage point or while traveling along a public highway, 39 waterway or path. Such elements may include natural and/or man-made landscape features, 40 for example landforms, land cover, water, landscaping, streetscapes, buildings and architectural 41 design elements. Scenic resources may be identified in the Underhill Town Plan, scenic resource 42 inventories, or through specific site analyses. 43 School: A public, private or parochial institution licensed by the State of Vermont to provide 1 educational instruction to students. Such facilities may also include accessory recreational and 2 dining facilities, and may be used as officially designated temporary emergency shelters (see 3

sections.title: ). See also Institutional Facility, Public Facility. 4
paragraphs: Setback: The horizontal distance from a road, lot line, boundary or other delineated feature 6 (e.g., a stream bank or channel, shoreline, or wetland area) to the nearest part of a building, 7 structure or use on a lot. In the case of a public highway, the distance shall be measured from 8 the nearest limit of the highway right-of-way (street line) or 25 feet from the centerline of the 9 highway, whichever is greater. In the case of a private road other than a driveway, the distance 10 shall be measured from the edge of the road right-of-way. 11 Sign: Any structure, display, device, material, object or representation which is designed or 13 used to advertise, direct or call attention to any property, establishment, business, enterprise, 14 profession, product, or service or other matter from any public right-of-way (see Section 3.16). 15 This definition includes words, lettering, figures, logos, trademarks, phrases, sentences, designs, 16 and other outdoor advertising displayed on natural objects, buildings, exterior walls and 17 windows, banners, canopies, fences or other manmade structures, which are visible from a 18 road right-of-way. For purposes of these regulations, a "permanent" sign is a sign that is on 19 display for 45 days or more in any one-year period. 20 Silviculture: See Forestry. 22 Site Disturbance: Removal of vegetation, grading, excavation, fill, or any combination thereof, 24 and site conditions resulting from such actions. See also Clearing. 25 Slope: The topographic gradient of any area of land, whether or not located on a single parcel, 27 as determined by the change in vertical distance or elevation (rise) over a horizontal distance 28 (run) which, for the purposes of these regulations is expressed as a percentage (e.g., 20-ft 29 gain/100-ft distance = 0.20 or 20%). For construction and grading purposes slope also may be 30 expressed as the ratio of the horizontal to vertical distance (e.g., 2:1). For purposes of these 31 regulations, a "steep slope" is a slope with a natural (pre-development) grade of 15% to 25%. A 32 "very steep slope" is a slope with a natural (pre-development) grade of more than 25% (see 33

Snack Bar: A seasonal roadside stand or enclosed structure, operated for a maximum of six (6) 36 months in any calendar year to include the summer months, for the preparation and sale of 37 food and beverages to the general public for consumption on- or off- the premises. A snack bar 38 shall include adequate off-street parking, and may include outdoor seating, as accessory to the 39 use. Indoor restaurant seating, and/or year-round use shall be allowed only as a permitted 40 restaurant. See also Restaurant. 41 Storage Facility: A building for storing goods as an accessory to a retail store, or for the 43 temporary storage of goods (e.g., household goods) by the general public. Self-storage facilities 44 are prohibited in the Town of Underhill, except as an Adaptive Reuse under Section 4.2. See 1 also Adaptive Reuse, Warehouse. 2 Story: That part of any building, excluding cellars and basements, between the surface of any 4 floor and the surface of the next floor above it, or if there is no floor above it, then the space 5 between a floor and the ceiling above it. See also Story, Half. 6 Story, Half: Any space partially within the roof framing, where the clear height of not more than 8 50% of such space between the top of the floor beams and the structural ceiling level is 7½ feet 9 or more. 10 Stream: Any surface water course in the Town of Underhill as depicted by the U.S. Geological 12 Survey on topographic maps, the Underhill Zoning Map, Vermont Base Map orthophotos, or as 13 identified through site investigation, but excluding artificially created irrigation and drainage 14 channels. This definition includes any stream channel two feet or more below the elevation of 15 surrounding land, with well defined stream banks, that directs the flow of surface water. See 16 also Stream Channel, Stream Banks. 17 Stream Channel: A defined area that demonstrates clear evidence of the permanent or 19 intermittent passage of water and includes, but may not be limited to bedrock channels, gravel 20 beds, sand and silt beds, and swales. A stream bank may define the usual boundaries, but not 21 the flood boundaries, of a stream channel. Artificially created water courses such as agricultural 22 irrigation and drainage ditches are specifically excluded from this definition. See also Stream, 23 Stream Bank. 24 Stream Bank: Physiographic feature that normally contains a stream within a channel. Stream 26 Banks are distinct from the streambed, which is normally wetted and provides a substrate that 27 supports aquatic organisms. For purposes of these regulations (see Section 3.19) "Top of Bank" 28 is defined as the point along a stream bank where an abrupt change in slope is evident, and 29 where the stream is generally able to overflow the banks and enter the adjacent floodplain only 30 during flows at or exceeding the average annual high water stage. "Top of Slope" is defined as 31 a break in the slope adjacent to steep-banked streams that have little or no floodplain. 32 Street: See Road. 34 Street Line: The dividing line between a lot and a public or private road or street, typically 36 defined by the edge of the road right-of-way. See also Front Lot Line. 37 Structure: An assembly of materials on the land for occupancy or use, including a building, 39 mobile home or trailer, sign, wall or fence. For purposes of these regulations "structure" also 40 includes but may not be limited to: additions to buildings, tennis courts, in-ground swimming 41 pools, telecommunications facilities, gas station canopies, and tanks for the outdoor storage of 42 gas or oil. Infrastructure, such as sidewalks, driveways, roads, parking areas, signs, service lines, 43 and the subsurface components of potable water and sewage disposal systems is specifically 44 excluded from this definition. Structures are exempted from these regulations only in 45 accordance with the Act [S4446] and these regulations (see Section 10.2). See also Accessory 1 Structure, Building, Improvement, Infrastructure. Also see "Structure" as defined for purposes 2 of flood hazard area management and regulation under Section 11.3. 3 Subdivider: Any person(s) who proposes to subdivide land, including an applicant for 5 subdivision approval. See also Applicant. 6 Subdivision: The division of any parcel of land into two or more parcels for the purpose of offer, 8 transfer, sale, conveyance, long-term lease or land development (see Section 7.2). The term 9 includes the re-subdivision of a previously subdivided parcel, amended subdivisions, the 10 division of land held in common among several owners, and planned unit development; and 11 any leaseholds equal to or exceeding 30 years or which, by right, may be extended to 30 years 12 or more. See also Boundary (Lot Line) Adjustment. 13 Subdivision, Major: A subdivision of land resulting in the creation of four (4) or more lots, and 15 all Planned Residential and Planned Unit Developments (see Section 7.2). 16 Subdivision, Minor: A boundary (lot line) adjustment, amendments to an approved subdivision 18 plan that will not substantially change the nature of the previously approved plan or conditions 19 of approval, or a subdivision which results in the creation of three or fewer lots (see Section 20 7.2). 21 Substantially Commenced: For purposes of these regulations, substantially commenced entails 23 the following: initial site preparation; the installation of an access; and the installation of a 24 foundation, water and/or wastewater system on-site, in accordance with these regulations and 25 all permits and approvals. 26 Substantially Complete: The completion of a permitted building or structure to the extent that 28 it may be safely occupied for its intended use. 29 Substantially Destroyed: Fifty percent (50%) or more of the structure has been damaged 31 and/or the damaged structure is no longer structurally sound, habitable or safe for its intended 32 use. 33 Transfer Station: A facility, including a recycling center, certified by the state that functions as a 35 collection point for solid waste and recyclable material that will subsequently be transported to 36 a state-approved landfill or disposal facility. The facility will include, at minimum, a receiving 37 hopper and compacting equipment (see Section 4.16). See also Public Facility. 38 Transit Facility: A building, structure, or area designed and intended for use by persons 40 changing transportation modes, including but not limited to bus and train stations. For 41 purposes of these regulations, this shall also include park and ride facilities which may also 42 provide access to other forms of public transportation. See also Parking Facility. 43 Tiny House: A type of single family dwelling or accessory dwelling that is typically less than 500 1 square feet. Whether the dwelling is mobile or non-mobile, a tiny house shall meet the same 2 standards as a dwelling meant for permanent occupation rather than temporary occupation. 3 For the purposes of these regulations, a mobile tiny house shall not be considered a camper, 4 recreation vehicle, or temporary shelter. See also Dwelling, Accessory; Principal Structure. 5 Undue Adverse Effect (Impact): An unnecessary or excessive impact that (1) violates a clear, 7 written community standard, including a provision of these regulations or a specific policy of 8 the municipal plan, or (2) which cannot be avoided through mitigation, alternative design, or 9 conditions of approval. 10 Use: The specific purpose for which a parcel of land or structure is designated, designed or 12 intended, or for which it may be used and maintained. See also Accessory Use, Structure. 13 Value-Added Production. Production activities that enhance or improve the overall value of 15 local agricultural or forestry products, including processing, packaging, direct marketing, and 16 related public outreach and educational activities. This may include the limited on-site sale of 17 goods produced on the premises, and directly related products, but shall not include general 18 retail sales. 19 Veterinary Clinic: A building or part thereof used for the care, diagnosis, treatment and 21 temporary boarding of animals. See also Kennel. 22 Warehouse Facility: A building used primarily for the storage, wholesale and distribution of 24 manufactured goods and materials, and not as a primary location or outlet for business or retail 25 uses. 26 Waste Management Facility: A public facility licensed or certified by the state of Vermont for 28 the collection, storage, transfer, shipment or disposal of solid or hazardous waste materials (see 29

sections.title: ), to include transfer stations, landfills, and other types of waste management 30
paragraphs: facilities, except for salvage yards (see Section 4.17). See also Public Facility, Salvage Yard. 31 Wetland: Those areas of the state which are inundated by surface or ground water with a 33 frequency sufficient to support vegetation or aquatic life that depend on saturated or 34 seasonally saturated soil conditions for growth and reproduction." Such areas include, but are 35 not limited to marshes, swamps, sloughs, potholes, fens, river and lake overflows, mud flats, 36 bogs and ponds, but exclude such areas where food and crops are grown in connection with 37 farming activities. The location of wetlands on a particular parcel, as indicated on State 38 Wetland Inventory Maps, shall be confirmed through site investigation unless waived by the 39 Development Review Board. 40 Wildlife Habitat: An ecological or environmental area that is inhabited by a particular species 42 of animal, plant or other type of organism. For purposes of these regulations, "significant" or 43 "critical" wildlife habitat includes: (1) "necessary wildlife habitat" as defined by the Vermont 44 Department of Fish and Wildlife (under 10 V.S.A. S6086(a)(8)(a)) to include habitat which is 45 concentrated, identifiable, and is demonstrated to be decisive to the survival of a species of 1 wildlife at any period in its life, including breeding and migration; (2) wildlife habitat identified 2 in the Underhill Town Plan and related maps and inventories as significant to the community; 3 and (3) wildlife habitat determined to be significant to the state, region or town, in consultation 4 with the Underhill Conservation Commission or the Vermont Department of Fish and Wildlife, 5 as identified through site-specific investigation. Applicants should refer to available information 6 on file at the Underhill Town Office and through the Vermont Department of Fish and Wildlife. 7 Wildlife Refuge: A designated area owned and/or managed by a public or nonprofit entity 9 principally for the purpose of sustaining wildlife habitat and/or wildlife populations, which may 10 also be open to the public for hunting and outdoor recreation. Designated trails and parking 11 areas, and storage and maintenance structures may be allowed as accessory to the principal 12 use. 13 Yard: An unoccupied area of ground, as defined by required setback distances, in which no 15 structure, building or portion thereof, may be located. See also Setback. 16 Yard Sale: See garage sale. 18

sections.title: Flood Hazard Area Regulation Definitions 20
paragraphs: Areas of Shallow Flooding: A designated AO or AH zone on a community's FIRM with a one 22 percent or greater annual chance of flooding to an average depth of one to three feet where a 23 clearly defined channel does not exist, where the path of flooding is unpredictable, and where 24 velocity flow may be evident. Such flooding is characterized by ponding or sheet flow. 25 Base Flood: The flood having a one percent (1%) chance of being equaled or exceeded in any 27 given year. 28 Base Flood Elevation (BFE): The elevation of the water surface elevation resulting from a flood 30 that has a one percent (1%) chance of equaling or exceeding that level in any given year. On 31 the Flood Insurance Rate Map the elevation is usually in feet, in relation to the National 32 Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929, the North American Vertical Datum of 1988, or other datum 33 referenced in the Flood Insurance Study report, or the average depth of the base flood, usually 34 in feet, above the ground surface. Base flood elevations are shown at selected intervals on 35 maps of Special Flood Hazard Areas that are determined by detailed methods. Base flood 36 elevations have not been determined in Zone A where the flood risk has been mapped by 37 approximate methods. 38 Construction/New: (a) For purposes of determining insurance rates pertaining to flood hazard 40 area regulation, structures that commenced on or after June 15, 1988 (the effective date of the 41 initial FIRM), and includes any subsequent improvements to such structures. (b) For floodplain 42 management purposes, new construction means structures for which the start of construction 43 commenced on or after the effective date of the floodplain management regulation adopted by 44 the Town of Underhill and includes any subsequent improvements to such structures. 45 Basement: Any area of building having its floor subgrade (below ground level) on all sides. 2 Building: See Structure. 4 Common Plan of Development: The approved plan or schedule for a structure to be 6 refurbished over a period of time. 7 Critical Public Facility: A facility critical to the health and safety of the public and the 9 environment, such as hospitals and nursing homes, emergency operations centers (particularly 10 police, fire, and rescue), vital data storage centers, power generation and other utilities 11 (including related infrastructure such as principal points of utility systems) and any facilities that 12 produce, use or store toxic pollutants as defined under the Clean Water Act and other state and 13 Federal statutes. New critical public facilities are prohibited within floodplains that is subject 14 either to a 1.0% or greater annual chance of flooding (the "100-year" floodplain) or a 0.2% or 15 greater annual chance of flooding (the "500-year" floodplain). 16 Development: Any man-made change to improved or unimproved real estate, including but 18 not limited to buildings or other structures, mining, dredging, filling, grading, paving, excavation 19 or drilling operations or storage of equipment or materials within the Special Flood Hazard 20 Area, identified on the most current Federal Insurance Rate Map (FIRM). 21 Flood: (a) a general and temporary condition of partial or complete inundation of normally dry 23 land areas from: the overflow of inland or tidal waters; the unusual and rapid accumulation of 24 runoff of surface waters from any source; and mudslides which are proximately caused by 25 flooding and are akin to a river of liquid and flowing mud on the surfaces of normally dry land 26 areas, as when earth is carried by a current of water and deposited along the path of the 27 current; (b) the collapse or subsidence of land along the shore of a lake or other body of water 28 as a result of erosion or undermining caused by waves or currents of water exceeding 29 anticipated cyclical levels or suddenly caused by an unusually high water level in a natural body 30 of water, accompanied by a severe storm, or by an unanticipated force of nature, such as flash 31 flood or abnormal tidal surge, or by some similarly unusual and unforeseeable event which 32 results in flooding. 33 Flood Hazard Boundary Map (FHBM): An official map of the community, issued by Federal 35 Emergency Management Agency, where the boundaries of the flood, mudslide (i.e., mudflow) 36 and related erosion areas having special hazards have been designated. 37 Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM): An official map of the community on which the Federal 39 Emergency Management Agency has delineated both the special hazard areas and the risk 40 premium zones applicable to the community. 41 Flood Insurance Study (FIS): An examination, evaluation, and determination of flood hazards 43 and, if appropriate, corresponding water surface elevations. 44 Floodplain or Flood-prone Area: Any land area susceptible to being inundated by water from 1 any source (also see Flood). 2 Floodproofed/Floodproofing: Any combination of structural and nonstructural additions, 4 changes or adjustments to structures that reduce or eliminate flood damage to real estate or 5 improved real property, water and sanitary facilities, structures and their contents. 6 Floodway (Regulatory in the Town of Underhill): The channel of a river or other watercourse 8 and the adjacent land areas that must be reserved in order to discharge the base flood without 9 cumulatively increasing the water surface elevation more than one foot at any point.
