Please 10 note, where floodways have been determined, they may be shown on separate map panels 11 from the Flood Insurance Rate Maps. 12 Fringe Area: The area outside of the floodway as shown on the Flood Insurance Rate Map, 14 which would be inundated by the hundred-year flood. 15 Functionally Dependent Use: A use which cannot perform its intended purpose unless it is 17 located or carried out in close proximity to water. 18 Historic Structure: Any structure that is: (1) listed individually in the National Register of 20 Historic Places (a listing maintained by the Department of the Interior) or preliminarily 21 determined by the Secretary of the Interior as meeting the requirements for individual listing 22 on the National Register; (2) certified or preliminarily determined by the Secretary of the 23 Interior as contributing to the historical significance of a registered historic district or a district 24 preliminarily determined by the Secretary to qualify as a registered historic district; (3) 25 individually listed on the state inventory of historic places; or (4) individually listed on a local 26 inventory of historic places in communities with historic preservation programs that have been 27 certified either: (a) by an approved state program as determined by the Secretary of the 28 Interior or (b) directly by the Secretary of the Interior in states without approved programs. 29 Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA): A letter issued by the Federal Emergency Management 31 Agency officially removing a structure or lot from the flood hazard zone based on information 32 provided by a certified engineer or surveyor. This is used where structures or lots are located 33 above the base flood elevation and have been inadvertently included in the mapped special 34 flood hazard area. 35 Lowest Floor: The lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area (including basement). An 37 unfinished or flood resistant enclosure, usable solely for parking of vehicles, building access or 38 storage in an area other than a basement area is not considered a building's lowest floor 39 provided that such enclosure is not built so as to render the structure in violation of the 40 applicable non-elevation design requirements of 44 CFR 60.3. 41 Manufactured (Mobile) Home: A structure, transportable in one or more sections, which is 43 built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling unit with or without a 44 permanent foundation when connected to required utilities. For floodplain management 45 purposes, the term "manufactured home" also includes park trailers, travel trailers, and other 1 similar recreational vehicles that are not fully licensed and ready for highway use. For flood 2 insurance purposes, the term "manufactured home" does not include park trailers, travel 3 trailers or other similar recreational vehicles. 4 Manufactured (Mobile) Home Park or Subdivision: A parcel (or contiguous parcels) of land 6 divided into two or more manufactured home lots for rent or sale. 7 Manufactured (Mobile) Home Park or Subdivision/Existing: A manufactured home park or 9 subdivision for which the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the 10 manufactured homes are to be affixed (including, at a minimum, the installation of utilities, the 11 construction of streets, and either final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads) is 12 completed before the effective date of initial floodplain management regulations adopted by 13 the town. 14 Manufactured (Mobile) Home Park or Subdivision/Expansion: The preparation of additional 16 sites by the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the manufacturing homes 17 are to be affixed (including the installation of utilities, the construction of streets, and either 18 final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads). 19 Manufactured (Mobile) Home Park or Subdivision/New: A manufactured home park or 21 subdivision for which the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the 22 manufactured homes are to be affixed (including at a minimum, the installation of utilities, the 23 construction of streets, and either final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads) is 24 completed on or after the effective date of the initial floodplain management regulations 25 adopted by the town. 26 Mean Sea Level: For purposes of the National Flood Insurance Program, the North American 28 Vertical Datum (NAVD 88) to which base flood elevations shown on a community's Flood 29 Insurance Rate Map are referenced. 30 Recreational Vehicle: For purposes of flood hazard area regulation, a vehicle which is: (a) built 32 on a single chassis; (b) 400 square feet or less when measured at the largest horizontal 33 projection; (c) designed to be self-propelled or permanently towable by a light duty truck; and 34 (d) designed primarily not for use as a permanent dwelling but as a temporary living quarters 35 for recreational, camping, travel, or seasonal use. 36 Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA): The land within a community subject to a one percent or 38 greater chance of flooding in any given year. This area is usually labeled Zone A, AO, AH, AE, 39 A1-30, or A99 in the most current flood insurance studies and on the maps published by the 40 Federal Emergency Management Agency. 41 Start of Construction: For purposes of flood hazard area regulation, determines the effective 43 maps or bylaw that regulated development in the Special Flood Hazard Area. The "start of 44 construction" includes substantial improvement, and means the date the building permit was 45 issued provided the actual start of construction, repair, reconstruction, rehabilitation, addition 1 placement, or other improvement was within 180 days of the permit date. The actual start 2 means either the first placement of permanent construction of a structure on a site, such as the 3 pouring of slab or footings, the installation of piles, the construction of columns, or any work 4 beyond the stage of excavation; or the placement of a manufactured home on a foundation. 5 Permanent construction does not include land preparation, such as clearing, grading, and filling; 6 nor does it include the installation of streets and/or walkways; nor does it include excavation 7 for a basement, footing, piers, or foundation or the erection of temporary forms; nor does it 8 include the installation on the property of accessory buildings, such as garages or shed not 9 occupied as dwelling units or not part of the main structure. For a substantial improvement, 10 the actual start of construction means the first alteration of any wall, ceiling, floor, or other 11 structural part of a building, regardless whether that alteration affects the external dimensions 12 of the building. 13 Structure: A walled and roofed building, as well as a manufactured (mobile) home, and any 15 related built systems, including gas or liquid storage tanks. 16 Substantial Damage: Damage of any origin sustained by a structure whereby the cost of 18 restoring the structure to its before-damaged condition would equal or exceed fifty percent of 19 the market value of the structure before the damage occurred. 20 Substantial Improvement: Any repair, reconstruction, or improvement of a structure, the cost 22 of which, over three years, or over the period of a common plan of development, cumulatively 23 equals or exceeds 50% of the market value of the structure either (a) before the improvement 24 or repair is started or (b) if the structure has been damaged, and is being restored, before the 25 damage occurred. The term does not, however, include either (a) any project for improvement 26 of the structure to comply with existing state or local health, sanitary, or safety code 27 specifications which are necessary to assure safe living conditions; or (b) any alteration of a 28 structure listed on the National Register of Historic Places or a state inventory of historic places. 29 Violation: The failure of a structure or other development to be fully compliant with these 31 regulations or conditions of permit approval. With respect to the flood hazard regulation, a 32 structure or other development without the elevation certificate, other certifications, or other 33 evidence of compliance required in 44 CFR 60.3 is presumed to be in violation until such time as 34 that documentation is provided. 35

sections.title: Telecommunications Facility Regulation Definitions 37
paragraphs: Adequate Coverage: Coverage is adequate within that area surrounding a base station where 39 the predicted or measured median field strength of the transmitted signal is such that the 40 majority of the time, transceivers properly installed and operated will be able to communicate 41 with the base station without objectionable noise (or excessive bit-error rate for digital) and 42 without calls being dropped. In the case of cellular communications in a rural environment like 43 Underhill, this would be a signal strength of at least -90 dBm. It is acceptable for there to be 44 holes within the area of adequate coverage, as long as the signal regains its strength farther 45 away from the base station. The outer boundary of the area of adequate coverage, however, is 1 that location past which the signal does not regain. 2 Affiliate: For the purposes of regulating telecommunications facilities, (1) when used in relation 4 to an operator, an affiliate is another person who directly or indirectly owns or controls, is 5 owned or controlled by, or is under common ownership or common control with the operator, 6 or an operator's principal partners, shareholders, or owners of some other ownership interest; 7 or (2) when used in relation to the municipality, an affiliate is any agency, board, authority or 8 political subdivision associated with the municipality or other person in which the municipality 9 has legal or financial interest. 10 Antenna: A device for transmitting and/or receiving electromagnetic signals. 12 Antenna Height: The vertical distance measured from the base of the antenna support 14 structure at grade to the highest point of the structure. If the support structure is on a sloped 15 grade, then the average between the highest and lowest grades at the base of the structure 16 shall be used in calculating the antenna height. 17 Antenna Support Structure: Any pole, telescoping mast, tower tripod, or any other structure 19 which supports a device used in the transmitting and/or receiving of electromagnetic signals. 20 Available Space: For purposes of regulating telecommunications facilities, the space on a 22 telecommunications tower or structure to which antennas of a telecommunications provider 23 are both structurally able and electromagnetically able to be attached. 24 Base Station: The primary sending and receiving site in a telecommunications facility network. 26 More than one base station and/or more than one variety of telecommunications provider can 27 be located on a single tower or structure. 28 Cellular Telecommunications: A commercial Low Power Mobile Radio Service bandwidth 30 licensed by the FCC to providers in a specific geographical area in which the radio frequency 31 spectrum is divided into discrete channels which are assigned in groups to geographic cells 32 within a service area and which are capable of being reused in different cells within the service 33 area. 34 Channel: For purposes of regulating telecommunications facilities, the segment of the 36 radiation spectrum to or from an antenna which carries one signal. An antenna may radiate on 37 many channels simultaneously. 38 Collocation: Locating wireless telecommunications equipment from more than one provider at 40 a single site or structure. 41 Common Carrier: An entity licensed by the FCC or a state agency to supply local and/or long 43 distance telecommunications services to the general public at established and stated rates. 44 dBm: Unit of measure of the power level of an electromagnetic signal at the input of a receiver, 1 given its antenna system gain at a particular frequency, expressed as decibels (dB) above one 2 milliwatt. Signal predictions with this measure are applicable at a particular frequency, and may 3 be ambiguous unless all receivers and antenna combinations utilize an identical frequency. 4 dBu: Unit of measure of the field intensity of an electromagnetic signal, expressed as decibels 6 (dB) above one microvolt per meter, an absolute measure for describing and comparing service 7 areas, independent of the many variables (see dBm) introduced by different receiver 8 configurations. This unit shall be used for coverage prediction plots 9 FCC: Federal Communications Commission. The federal government agency responsible for 11 regulating telecommunications in the United States. 12 Hertz: (Hz) One hertz is the frequency of an electric or magnetic field which reverses polarity 14 once each second, or one cycle per second. 15 Interference: An undesirable effect caused by electromagnetic signals. FCC "Type 1" 17 interference refers to interference regulated by the FCC and affecting other FCC licensees or 18 other entities over which the FCC has jurisdiction. FCC "Type 2" interference refers to 19 electromagnetic disturbances to business, institutional, medical, and home electronic 20 equipment. 21 Location: For purposes of regulating telecommunications facilities, references to site location 23 shall be the exact longitude and latitude, to the nearest tenth of a second. Bearing or 24 orientation should be referenced to true north. 25 Modification of an Existing Telecommunications Facility: Any change, or proposed change, in 27 power input or output, number of antennas, change in antenna type(s) or model(s), 28 repositioning of antenna(s), or change in number of channels per antenna above the maximum 29 number approved under an existing permit. 30 Modification of an Existing Telecommunications Tower or Structure: Any change, or proposed 32 change, in dimensions of an existing and permitted tower or other structure designed to 33 support telecommunications transmission, receiving and/or relaying antennas and/or 34 equipment. 35 Monitoring: The ongoing observation or measurement of existing conditions, through site 37 inspections and the use of instruments in the field. 38 Monitoring Protocol: For purposes of regulating and monitoring telecommunications facilities, 40 the testing protocol, such as the Cobbs Protocol , or the FCC Regulations (Title 47, Part 1, 41

sections.title: referenced as IEEE C95.3 1991), or one substantially similar, including 42
paragraphs: compliance determined in accordance with the National Council on Radiation Protection and 43 Measurements, (Reports 86 and 119) which is to be used to monitor the emissions and 44 determine exposure risk from existing and new telecommunications facilities. 45 Monopole: A single self-supporting vertical pole with no guy wire anchors, usually consisting of 2 a galvanized or other unpainted metal or a wooden pole with below-grade foundations. 3 Radial Plots: Radial plots are the result of drawing equally spaced lines (radials) from the point 5 of the antenna, calculating the expected signal and indicating this graphically on a map. The 6 relative signal strength may be indicated by varying the size or color at each point being studied 7 along the radial. A threshold plot uses a mark to indicate whether that point would be strong 8 enough to provide adequate coverage i.e., the points meeting the threshold of adequate 9 coverage. The draw back is the concentration of points close to the antenna and the divergence 10 of points far from the site near the ends of the radials. 11 Repeater: A small receiver/relay transmitter and antenna of relatively low power output 13 designed to provide service to areas which are not able to receive adequate coverage directly 14 from a base or primary station. 15 Roof and/or Building Mount Telecommunications Facility: A telecommunications facility in 17 which antennas are mounted to an existing structure on the roof (including rooftop 18 appurtenances) or a building face. 19 Structurally Able: For purposes of regulating telecommunications facilities, the determination 21 that a tower or structure is capable of safely carrying the load imposed by the proposed new 22 antenna(s) under all reasonably predictable conditions as determined by professional structural 23 engineering analysis including the wind load or any other structural requirements. 24 Telecommunications Equipment Shelter: A structure located at a base station designed 26 principally to enclose equipment used in connection with telecommunications transmissions 27 including any foundation that may be required. 28 Telecommunications Facility: (1) As defined under the Act [S4303(29)] for purposes of these 30 regulations: "A tower or other support structure, including antennae, that will extend 20 or 31 more feet vertically, and related equipment; and base structures to be used primarily for 32 communication or broadcast purposes to transmit or receive communication or broadcast 33 signals." (2) If regulated by the Vermont Public Service Board [30 V.S.A. S248a], and therefore 34 exempted from these regulations: "A communications facility that transmits and receives 35 signals to and from a local, state, national, or international network used primarily for two-way 36 communications for commercial, industrial, municipal, county, or state purposes and any 37 associated support structure that is proposed for construction or installation which is primarily 38 for communications purposes, and any ancillary improvements that are proposed for 39 construction or installation and are primarily intended to serve the communications facilities or 40 support structure." 41 Telecommunications Facility Site: A property, or any part thereof, which is owned or leased by 43 one or more telecommunications providers and upon which one or more telecommunications 44 facilities and any required landscaping are located. See also Subdivision. 45 Telecommunications Provider: An entity licensed by the FCC to provide telecommunications 2 services to individuals or institutions. 3 Telecommunications Tower: A guyed, monopole, or self-supporting tower, constructed as a 5 free-standing structure or in association with a building, other permanent structure or 6 equipment, containing one or more antennas intended for transmitting and/or receiving 7 television, AM/FM radio, digital, microwave, cellular, telephone, or similar forms of electronic 8 communication. 9 Temporary Wireless Telecommunications Facility: Any tower, pole, antenna, or other facility 10 designed for use while a permanent wireless telecommunications facility is under construction, 11 rehabilitation or restoration. 12 Tiled Coverage Plots: Tiled plots result from calculating the signal at uniformly spaced locations 14 on a rectangular grid, or tile, of the area of concern. Tiled plots (in comparison to radial plots) 15 (1) provide a uniform distribution of points over the area of interest, (2) usually allow the same 16 grid to be used as different sites are examined, and (3) do not necessitate the transmitter site 17 be within the grid or area of interest. As with radial plots, the graphic display or plot can be 18 either signal strength or adequate threshold. Tile plotting requires more topographic data and 19 longer (computer) execution time than radial plotting, but is preferable for comparative 20 analysis. 21
